note: Measures the shared-memory capture transport end to end, which until now had no CLI route: `PortalCapture` took `transport=` but no caller passed it, so `--capture-transport shm` (wired this pass in minimal/__main__.py and minimal/capture.py) puts the chain's end on `fdsink fd=<memfd>` and reads each frame with one pread instead of ~8 through the 1 MiB pipe. The argv is r2026-11-08-1080p-window-c's with `--capture-transport shm` added, so the pair is one variable apart. What that run read, and what this one has to beat: **30.5 ms / 32.8 fps steady, capture split wait 0.5 / read 5.1 ms**, gst chain 25% of one core. The reading is `read`, which should fall toward a memory copy while the frame time holds or improves; the `capture cpu:` line is the second reading. The caps are unchanged (RGBA 1920x1080), so the before/after PNG hashes are the check that the transport changed no pixel - a changed hash is a defect, not a trade. If `read` does not fall, the transport is settled as not the lever and the capture leg is closed for good. `manual: true` because the window source wants a picker clicked.
